title: 3D generation: meshes, SDFs, voxels and Gaussian splats

questions.q: The exposed-face area of a voxel sphere is about 1.5 times the truth. What happens with a grid twice as fine?
options: It stays about 1.5: smaller stairs have the same total
questions.answer: It stays about 1.5: smaller stairs have the same total
questions.why: Stairs sum to the sphere's shadows on three axes from two sides, 6πr². The lab reads 1.511, 1.507 and 1.500.

questions.q: What does a signed distance function give you that plain occupancy doesn't?
options: A value that lets you interpolate where the surface lies between samples
Lower memory at the same grid
questions.answer: A value that lets you interpolate where the surface lies between samples
questions.why: Occupancy only says in or out. The lab's SDF finds radius 1.0000 from 8 samples, where occupancy says 1.1250.

questions.q: Why do sparse grids and narrow bands save so much?
options: A surface grows with the square of resolution, while a full grid grows with the cube
questions.answer: A surface grows with the square of resolution, while a full grid grows with the cube
questions.why: Most cells are air or solid. Keeping only cells near the surface follows the smaller growth.

questions.q: What can't a Gaussian splat give you directly?
options: A closed surface for printing or physics
questions.answer: A closed surface for printing or physics
questions.why: A splat is soft blobs without triangles or an inside. Convert with SplatToMesh and accept the loss.

questions.q: Which node turns a decoded grid into triangles?
questions.why: VoxelToMesh takes VOXEL and gives MESH. DecimateMesh takes a mesh already made.
